claim: Skeletal muscle biopsies were collected from 60 healthy participants of the Genetic and Epigenetic Study of Aging Laboratory Testing (GESTALT) aged 20 to 87 years.
source: Skeletal muscle biopsies were collected from 60 healthy participants of the Genetic and Epigenetic Study of Aging Laboratory Testing (GESTALT) aged 20 to 87 years who were defined as 'healthy' based on very strict evaluation criteria at the National Institute on Aging Clinical Unit in Baltimore (Tanaka et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of participants, study name, age range, and health status criteria.

claim: Using multiplexed isobaric labeling tags (TMT) and a customized analytical strategy, 5891 proteins were quantified from 400,000 tryptic peptides from 6.7 million spectra.
source: Using multiplexed isobaric labeling tags (TMT) and a customized analytical strategy (Kammers et al., 2015; Herbrich et al., 2013), we identified 400,000 tryptic peptides from 6.7 million spectra (396 multiplexed MS runs from 12 TMT 6-plex experiments), which allowed the quantification of 5891 proteins (Figure 1—source data 1, PXD011967).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data from the proteomic analysis and cites methodological references.

claim: Of the initial 5891 proteins detected, 1511 proteins were excluded from the analysis because they were not quantifiable in at least three participants per age strata.
source: Of the initial 5891 proteins detected, we excluded from the analysis 1511 proteins that were not quantifiable in at least three participants per age strata (at least 15 participants total) and performed the analysis in the remaining 4380 proteins detected in more than 15 donors (three per age strata), which were quantified from 46,834 unique peptides and 2.7 million spectra (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the exclusion criteria and resulting protein count for analysis.

claim: There were 1265 proteins significantly associated with age (p<0.05, with BH correction <0.1, 917 proteins), suggesting that approximately 29% of the skeletal muscle proteome changed with aging after 20 years of age.
source: There were 1265 proteins significantly associated with age (p<0.05, with BH correction <0.1, 917 proteins), suggesting that approximately 29% of the skeletal muscle proteome changed with aging after 20 years of age (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific statistical results with p-values and correction methods.

claim: Of the 1265 age-associated proteins, 29% (361) were significantly underrepresented and 71% (904) were overrepresented with older age.
source: Of these, 29% (361) were significantly underrepresented and 71% (904) were overrepresented with older age.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the percentage and number of proteins in each category.

claim: LSm14A was the protein most strongly associated with older age (β = 0.023, p=0.0109).
source: Notably, the proteins most strongly associated with older age (Figure 1A, right) were LSM14 homolog A (LSm14A, β = 0.023, p=0.0109), tissue metalloproteinase inhibitor 3 (TIMP-3, β = 0.0219, p=0.00026) and serum amyloid P-component (APCS, β = 0.0164, p=1.26E-11).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, and references Figure 1A.

claim: Protein LSm14A is implicated in processing the assembly of processing bodies, involved in mRNA turnover, and can also bind to viral nucleic acids and initiate IFN-β production, contributing to innate immunity.
source: Protein LSm14A is implicated in processing the assembly of processing bodies, involved in mRNA turnover, and can also bind to viral nucleic acids and initiate IFN-β production, contributing to innate immunity (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript describes the biological function of LSm14A and cites a reference.

claim: TIMP3 regulates the adipogenic differentiation of fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) in skeletal muscle, and its overrepresentation may explain the tendency for fat infiltration in aging muscle.
source: TIMP3 regulates the adipogenic differentiation of fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) in skeletal muscle, and its overrepresentation may explain the tendency for fat infiltration in aging muscle (Kopinke et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript describes the function of TIMP3 and provides a speculative interpretation with a citation.

claim: APCS is indicative of systemic amyloid, and its overrepresentation in aging muscle has never been previously described.
source: APCS is indicative of systemic amyloid, and its overrepresentation in aging muscle has never been previously described.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this is a novel finding.

claim: The most underrepresented protein with old age was HLA class II histocompatibility antigen (HLA-DRB1, p=0.024).
source: The most underrepresented proteins (age β <−0.01 and p<0.05) with old age (Figure 1A, left) were HLA class II histocompatibility antigen (HLA-DRB1, p=0.024), dedicator of cytokinesis protein 4 (DOCK4, p=0.025), myosin-binding protein H (MYBPH, p=0.0005), and microfibril-associated glycoprotein 4 (MFAP4, p=0.000002).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific p-values and references Figure 1A.

claim: MYBPH maintains the structural integrity of the muscle and its decreased expression has been associated with muscle weakness in age-related disorders.
source: MYBPH maintains the structural integrity of the muscle and its decreased expression has been associated with muscle weakness in age-related disorders (Hundley et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript describes the function of MYBPH and cites a reference.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of protein expression suggested that the strongest difference was between young (20-34) and old (80+).
source: Hierarchical clustering of protein expression suggested that the strongest difference was between young (20-34) and old (80+).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the result of hierarchical clustering analysis.

claim: There were small differences in protein expression before the age of 50, but afterwards there was on average three log fold protein expression differences, and even more substantial differences after the age of 64.
source: There were small differences before the age of 50, but afterwards there was on average three log fold protein expression differences, and even more substantial differences after the age of 64.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative differences in protein expression across age ranges.

claim: The fiber ratio of slow/fast was higher with older age (p=0.005).
source: as expected, the fiber ratio of slow/fast was higher with older age (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 A5). The slight change of slow/fast fiber ratio was significant and outweighed the wide variability among individuals (p=0.005)
evidence: The manuscript provides a specific p-value and references a figure.

claim: The top 95 contractile proteins involved in the architectural and functional stabilization of the sarcomere decreased with age.
source: Since many proteins decreasing with age were contractile proteins, we classified these further by function. The top 95 proteins in this class are involved in the architectural and functional stabilization of the sarcomere, including sarcospan (SSPN, β = 0.002, p=0.016) (Figure 1E), a dystrophin-associated protein complex important for muscle regeneration, actin-binding LIM domain and actin-binding protein 1 (LIMA1, β = 0.003, p=0.009), a cytoskeleton-binding protein that stabilizes actin filaments, and plectin (PLEC, β = 0.0007, p=0.036), a large cytoskeleton protein that preserves interactions within the acto-myosin complex.
evidence: The manuscript describes specific proteins with beta coefficients and p-values, and references Figure 1E.

claim: Increases in delta sarcoglycan (SGCD, β = 0.0019, p=0.00004), and gamma sarcoglycan (SGCG, β = 0.0016, p=0.0062) were consistent with mouse studies showing that dystrophin, sarcoglycan subcomplex γ- and δ-sarcoglycan were overexpressed with aging.
source: Increases in delta sarcoglycan (SGCD, β = 0.0019, p=0.00004), and gamma sarcoglycan (SGCG, β = 0.0016, p=0.0062) were consistent with mouse studies showing that dystrophin, sarcoglycan subcomplex γ- and δ-sarcoglycan were overexpressed with aging, perhaps a compensatory mechanism to avoid damage in the sarcomere during contraction or as biomarkers of continuous repair (Hughes et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific data and compares it to mouse studies with a citation.

claim: MAPT (tau) was significantly underrepresented in older muscle.
source: Interestingly, MAPT (tau, mostly expressed in neurons and involved in the assembly and stabilization of microtubules), was also significantly underrepresented in older muscle (Figure 1E).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: The levels of Syne-1 which anchors both synaptic and non-synaptic myonuclei for proper neuron innervation and respiration increased with age (SYNE1 β = 0.002, p=0.005).
source: By contrast, the levels of Syne-1 which anchors both synaptic and non-synaptic myonuclei for proper neuron innervation and respiration increased with age (SYNE1 β = 0.002, p=0.005) as did beta-2-syntrophin, which is believed to be involved in acetylcholine receptor clustering (SNTB2, β = 0.0029, p=0.0003).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values.

claim: The coverage of mitochondrial proteins quantified by the analysis ranged from 92% for TCA proteins to 52% for proteins located in outer mitochondrial membrane.
source: The coverage of mitochondrial proteins quantified by our analysis compared to those described in the literature ranged from 92% for TCA proteins to 52% for proteins located in outer mitochondrial membrane [possibly due to incomplete tissue disruption (Morgenstern et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2014)] (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages and references a figure and citations.

claim: Of the mitochondrial proteins identified, the abundance of 25% of them (173 proteins) changed with age, mostly (70%) declining with age.
source: Of the mitochondrial proteins identified, the abundance of 25% of them (173 proteins) changed with age, mostly (70%) declining with age.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages and numbers.

claim: NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase 3 (CYB5R3), an NADH‐dehydrogenase located in the outer membrane of ER and mitochondria, whose overexpression is known to mimic many effects of caloric restriction, was significantly overrepresented in older age.
source: Notably, however, outer membrane proteins were more abundant (Figure 2B); for example, NADH-cytochrome b5 reductase 3 (CYB5R3), an NADH‐dehydrogenase located in the outer membrane of ER and mitochondria, whose overexpression is known to mimic many effects of caloric restriction, was significantly overrepresented in older age (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) (Martin-Montalvo et al., 2016; Diaz-Ruiz et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript describes the protein, its function, and provides citations.

claim: Of the enzymatic mitochondrial proteins, 99 were respiratory chain proteins (Complex I-V and assembly complex proteins), and most of them declined with aging (28 proteins p<0.05).
source: Of the enzymatic mitochondrial proteins, 99 were respiratory chain proteins (Complex I-V and assembly complex proteins), and most of them declined with aging (28 proteins p<0.05; Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers and p-values, and references a figure.

claim: Succinate dehydrogenase complex assembly factor 2 (SDHAF2), required for covalent FAD insertion into complex II, was significantly overrepresented with older age.
source: Surprisingly, succinate dehydrogenase complex assembly factor 2 (SDHAF2), required for covalent FAD insertion into complex II, the electron transport chain, and the TCA cycle, were significantly overrepresented with older age (Figure 2C inset).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Of 22 proteins quantified for TCA cycle, only malate dehydrogenase (MDH1), isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1), fumarate hydratase (FH) and succinate--CoA ligase (SUCLG1) were significantly lower at older ages.
source: Of 22 proteins quantified for TCA cycle, only malate dehydrogenase (MDH1), isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1), fumarate hydratase (FH) and succinate--CoA ligase (SUCLG1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) were significantly lower at older ages.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific protein names and references a figure.

claim: NNT (NAD(P) transhydrogenase) significantly decreased with aging (β = −0.003, p=0.001).
source: In addition, to IDH1, NADP+ is also reduced to NADPH via the mitochondrial NAD(P)-malic enzyme (ME2) (Sauer et al., 2004) and predominantly through NNT (NAD(P) transhydrogenase) and the pentose phosphate pathway. In our study, NNT (β = −0.003, p=0.001) significantly decreased with aging.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and cites a reference.

claim: NADK (NAD+ Kinase), which is highly regulated by the redox state of the cell and regulates NADP+ synthesis in vivo decreased with age (NADK2, β = −0.001, p=0.052).
source: Further, NADK (NAD+ Kinase), which is highly regulated by the redox state of the cell and regulates NADP+ synthesis in vivo decreased with age (NADK2, β = −0.001, p=0.052).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value.

claim: NAM-N-methyl transferase (NNMT, β = 0.007, p=0.016), nicotinamide ribose kinases (NMRK1, β = −0.003, p=0.002), poly-ADP-ribose polymerases (PARP1, β = 0.002, p=0.003) and CD73 (NT5E, β = 0.004, p=0.056) were significantly increased with older ages.
source: We found that NAM-N-methyl transferase (NNMT, β = 0.007, p=0.016), nicotinamide ribose kinases (NMRK1, β = −0.003, p=0.002), poly-ADP-ribose polymerases (PARP1, β = 0.002, p=0.003) and CD73 (NT5E, β = 0.004, p=0.056) were significantly increased with at older ages, while only NMRK1 decreased with age (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, and references a figure.

claim: Most genomic maintenance proteins increased in abundance with age, especially those involved in DNA damage recognition and repair.
source: Most genomic maintenance proteins increased in abundance with age, especially those involved in DNA damage recognition and repair, such as double-strand break repair protein (MRE11), X-ray repair cross-complementing protein 5 (XRCC5), and structural maintenance of chromosomes protein 1A (SMC1A) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Prelamin-A/C (LMNA), Lamin-B1 (LMNB1) and Lamin-B2 (LMNB2), members of the LMN family of protein components of nuclear lamina, were all overrepresented with older age.
source: Prelamin-A/C (LMNA), Lamin-B1 (LMNB1) and Lamin-B2 (LMNB2), members of the LMN family of protein components of nuclear lamina that help maintain nuclear and genome architecture, were all overrepresented with older age (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Sirtuin 2 (SIRT2, β = −0.0013, p=0.032), implicated in genomic stability, metabolism and aging, was found to be lower in older skeletal muscle.
source: Sirtuin 2 (SIRT2, β = −0.0013, p=0.032), implicated in genomic stability, metabolism and aging, was also found to be lower in older skeletal muscle (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and references a figure.

claim: Forty proteins that have been implicated in cellular senescence were significantly overrepresented with age.
source: Forty proteins that in the literature have been implicated in cellular senescence were significantly overrepresented with age.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding.

claim: Of all the 69 age-associated transcription-regulatory proteins quantified, 61 were overrepresented and only eight were underrepresented with older age.
source: Of all the 69 age-associated transcription-regulatory proteins quantified, 61 were overrepresented and only eight were underrepresented with older age.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers.

claim: Kelch-like protein 31 (KLHL31, β = −0.0017, p=0.003), which is essential for muscle development and perhaps also muscle repair, was underrepresented with older age.
source: This last subset included kelch-like protein 31 (KLHL31, β = −0.0017, p=0.003), which is essential for muscle development and perhaps also muscle repair (Abou-Elhamd et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and cites a reference.

claim: The levels of myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D (MEF2D, β = 0.003, p=0.018), essential for myogenesis and muscle regeneration and the primary regulator of KLHL31 production, increased.
source: Of note, the levels of myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D (MEF2D, β = 0.003, p=0.018), essential for myogenesis and muscle regeneration and the primary regulator of KLHL31 production, increased, possibly as a compensatory mechanism (Schiaffino et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and cites a reference.

claim: CTCF (β = 0.009, p=0.026), a transcriptional activator and repressor protein that fine-tunes chromatin architecture, increased with age.
source: Contrary to earlier reports, CTCF (β = 0.009, p=0.026), a transcriptional activator and repressor protein that fine-tunes chromatin architecture, also increased with age (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and references a figure.

claim: Of the ~300 spliceosome proteins and spliceosome-associated factors described, 99 and 57 of them, respectively, were overrepresented in older muscle.
source: In particular, of the ~300 proteins and spliceosome-associated factors described (Zhou et al., 2002; Rappsilber et al., 2002), we found that 99 and 57 of them, respectively, were overrepresented in older muscle (Figure 3C).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers and cites references.

claim: Spliceosomal proteins increased by ~15% between the ages of 20 and 87 years.
source: Overall, spliceosomal proteins increased by ~15% between the ages of 20 and 87 years (Figure 3D).
evidence: The manuscript provides a specific percentage and references a figure.

claim: LSm RNA-binding protein (LSM14A) was the most overrepresented assembly protein, displaying a 20-fold increase with age.
source: LSm RNA-binding protein (LSM14A) was the most overrepresented assembly protein, displaying a 20-fold increase with age.
evidence: The manuscript provides a specific fold-change value.

claim: Analysis of 144,830 transcripts from RNA-seq datasets showed that around 3.7% of the skeletal muscle transcripts (5459 transcripts, corresponding to 6255 events) showed relative abundance changes with aging.
source: Analysis of 144,830 transcripts from RNA-seq datasets showed that around 3.7% of the skeletal muscle transcripts (5459 transcripts, corresponding to 6255 events) showed relative abundance changes with aging (Figure 4A; Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers and percentages, and references a figure.

claim: 2714 splicing events were significantly less frequent at older ages and 3545 events significantly more frequent at older ages.
source: Next, we calculated the frequency and distribution of splicing events with aging as well as the directionality of such changes and found that 2714 events were significantly less frequent at older ages and 3545 events significantly more frequent at older ages (Figure 4B; Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers and references a figure.

claim: AS events increased significantly with age (r2 = 0.33, p=6.001e-06).
source: The overall number of events increased slightly with older age but AS events, at least for the 6,255 AS events quantified, increased significantly with age (r2 = 0.33, p=6.001e-06) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific statistical values and references a figure.

claim: Among the 5459 transcripts that were alternatively spliced with age, 4967 transcripts were protein-coding.
source: Among the 5459 transcripts (from 3791 genes) that were alternatively spliced with age, 4967 transcripts were protein-coding.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numbers.

claim: 8.9% of the age-associated alternatively spliced transcripts (385) were reflected in protein changes.
source: We compared these genes with the age-associated proteins and found that 8.9% of the age-associated alternatively spliced transcripts (385) were reflected in protein changes (Figure 4E).
evidence: The manuscript provides a specific percentage and number, and references a figure.

claim: 30% (385) of the age-associated proteins undergo alternative splicing.
source: This comparison of age-associated proteins and alternatively splicing mRNAs suggests that 30% (385) of the age-associated proteins undergo alternative splicing.
evidence: The manuscript provides a specific percentage and number.

claim: All the 60S and 40S ribosomal proteins were globally reduced in older muscle.
source: In particular, all the 60S and 40S ribosomal proteins were globally reduced in older muscle; exceptions included 60S ribosomal proteins RPL12 and RPL3 (RPL12, β = 0.0008, p=0.024, RPL3, β = 0.003, p=0.016), as well as H/ACA ribonucleoprotein complex subunit 4 (DKC1, β = 0.002, p=0.034) and nucleolar protein 58 (NOP58, β = 0.003, p=0.00007), which were overrepresented in old muscle.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding with specific exceptions.

claim: Of the 239 detected proteins related to proteostasis, 31% were altered with age (p<0.05, 24 underrepresented and 50 overrepresented with older age).
source: Of the 239 detected proteins that has been related to proteostasis in the literature, 31% were altered with age (p<0.05, 24 underrepresented and 50 overrepresented with older age) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages and numbers, and references a figure.

claim: Most proteins underrepresented with age were chaperones, including DnaJ homolog subfamily A (DNAJA1), also named heat shock protein (Hsp) 40 (β = −0.0021, p=0.003), Hsp27 (β = −0.004, p=0.0001), Hsp70 protein 8 (HSPA8, β = −0.002, p=2.34E-07).
source: Most proteins underrepresented with age were chaperones, including DnaJ homolog subfamily A (DNAJA1), also named heat shock protein (Hsp) 40 (β = −0.0021, p=0.003), Hsp27 (β = −0.004, p=0.0001), Hsp70 protein 8 (HSPA8, β = −0.002, p=2.34E-07) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) as well as Hsp27 protein 1 (HSPB1) and protein 7 (HSPB7), Hsp10 protein 1 (HSPE1) and Hsp60 protein 1 (HSPD1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, and references a figure.

claim: Most proteostasis proteins overrepresented with aging were related to autophagy except HSPA8 and Eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4 gamma 1 (EIF4G1).
source: Indeed, most proteostasis proteins overrepresented with aging were related to autophagy except HSPA8 and Eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4 gamma 1 (EIF4G1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding.

claim: TDP-43, a DNA/RNA-binding protein that tends to form aggregates in tissues such as skeletal muscle and brain, increased significantly with aging (TARDBP, β = 0.002, p=0.0002).
source: For example, TDP-43, a DNA/RNA-binding protein that tends to form aggregates in tissues such as skeletal muscle and brain and is both removed by autophagy and involved in autophagy maintenance, increased significantly with aging (TARDBP, β = 0.002, p=0.0002) (Figure 5D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and references a figure.

claim: Calreticulin (CALR), a quality control chaperone induced under ER stress that stimulated autophagy, was significantly higher in muscle of older participants (β = 0.001, p=0.022).
source: On the contrary, calreticulin (CALR), a quality control chaperone induced under ER stress that stimulated autophagy, was significantly higher in muscle of older participants (β = 0.001, p=0.022) (Figure 5D) (Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, references a figure, and cites a reference.

claim: Of the 32 immune-related age-associated proteins that were quantified, many proteins previously linked to macrophage function (such as CD14, LGALS3, CAPG, INPPL1 and MAST2) were dysregulated in aging muscle.
source: Of the 32 immune-related age-associated proteins that were quantified (Figure 6A), three broad themes emerged from the aging muscle immune proteome (Figure 6B–D). First, many proteins previously linked to macrophage function (such as CD14, LGALS3, CAPG, INPPL1 and MAST2) were dysregulated in aging muscle, with skewing towards a pro-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references figures.

claim: Monocyte differentiation antigen CD14 (CD14, β = 0.003, p=0.009), Interferon-induced, double-stranded RNA-activated protein kinase (E2AK2, β = 0.0008 p=0.046) and ASC (PYCARD) (β = 0.006, p=0.025) were overrepresented with aging.
source: For example, the overrepresentation with aging of proteins such as Monocyte differentiation antigen CD14 (CD14, β = 0.003, p=0.009), Interferon-induced, double-stranded RNA-activated protein kinase (E2AK2, β = 0.0008 p=0.046) and ASC (PYCARD) (β = 0.006, p=0.025) can be viewed as being pro-inflammatory via their proposed role in lipid sensing and NF-κB activation (Figure 6B.1) (Bryan et al., 2009; Sarkar et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, references a figure, and cites references.

claim: Microtubule-associated serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (MAST2, β = −0.002, p=0.023) and Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 5-phosphatase 2 (INPPL1, β = −0.0009, p=0.036) were downregulated with aging.
source: Interestingly, we also identified proteins that were concurrently downregulated, such as Microtubule-associated serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (MAST2, β = −0.002, p=0.023) and Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 5-phosphatase 2 (INPPL1, β = −0.0009, p=0.036), that could accentuate the inflammatory phenotype by attenuating the negative regulation of NF-κB (Figure 6B.2) (Kalesnikoff et al., 2002; Tridandapani et al., 2002).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, references a figure, and cites references.

claim: High mobility group protein B2 (HMGB2, β = 0.004, p=0.001), a well-known 'alarmin', increased with aging.
source: We also noted increased expression of high mobility group protein B2 (HMGB2, β = 0.004, p=0.001), a well-known 'alarmin' (Taniguchi et al., 2018) that is released from dying cells or within neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), that may further exacerbate the inflammatory milieu.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and cites a reference.

claim: Annexin A1 (ANXA1, β = 0.008, p=0.00001), a protein that has been linked to resolution of inflammation, showed strong age-associated upregulation.
source: This was most evident in strong age-associated upregulation of annexin A1 (ANXA1, β = 0.008, p=0.00001), a protein that has been linked to resolution of inflammation (Gobbetti and Cooray, 2016).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and cites a reference.

claim: Elevated levels of adiponectin (ADIPOQ, β = 0.002, p=0.008), a chemokine produced exclusively by adipocytes, likely reflected increased adipogenic activity in aging muscle.
source: Elevated levels of adiponectin (ADIPOQ, β = 0.002, p=0.008), a chemokine produced exclusively by adipocytes, likely reflected increased adipogenic activity in aging muscle.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value, and offers an interpretation.

claim: Coordinate upregulation of several members of the alternate complement pathway, such as CFAH (β = 0.003, p=0.028), and CFAD (β = 0.003, p=0.039) and modulators of complement activity such as CD antigen CD55 (DAF and CD55, β = 0.006, p=0.00007) indicate ongoing innate immune activity in aging muscle.
source: Third, coordinate upregulation of several members of the alternate complement pathway, such as CFAH (β = 0.003, p=0.028), and CFAD (β = 0.003, p=0.039) and modulators of complement activity such as CD antigen CD55 (DAF and CD55, β = 0.006, p=0.00007) indicate ongoing innate immune activity in aging muscle (Figure 6D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficients and p-values, and references a figure.

claim: Immunoglobulin heavy constant gamma 4 (IGHG4, β = 0.008, p=0.019) increased with age.
source: The latter could be mediated, for example, by Immunoglobulin heavy constant gamma 4 (IGHG4, β = 0.008, p=0.019) which we found to be increased with age.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific beta coefficient and p-value.
